params.prompt: Start from the exact composition of the start image: a close-up smile with braces. The woman stays still and keeps smiling calmly. The camera performs one single slow, smooth, continuous lateral pan to the left, moving away from her mouth. Her smile gradually slides out of the right side of the frame. As the camera keeps panning left, a pair of dental extraction forceps already holding the extracted tooth comes into view from the left side of the frame, in front of a soft, blurred dark grey-blue clinic background. The forceps and the tooth are already outside the mouth from the very beginning: nothing is pulled out of the mouth, cheek or face, there is no extraction action, the forceps never touch the woman, and the tooth never emerges from her body. The camera simply discovers the tooth in the forceps beside her. The camera slows down and settles on the exact composition of the end image: the forceps with the tooth in sharp focus, background blurred. RULES: 16:9, photorealistic premium clinical cinematography. Slow, gradual pan with a subtle focus shift; no cuts, fades, black frames, zooms, rotations, flicker, warping or morphing. Nothing appears out of nowhere or materializes; the forceps simply enter the frame because the camera moves. No blood, no extra hands or people, no text or logos. Preserve the braces, teeth, forceps and tooth exactly as in the references. End exactly on the end image composition.
